artifact: A1.2 scientific execution and adoption request v11
review_boundary: Artifact-only review of a local preparation request. No provider, protected payload, measured retrieval, model, or external evidence was accessed.

overall.one_line_summary: The repaired v11 package is a coherent, fail-closed request for later Owner review, but it is not adoption, execution authority, or measured evidence.
strengths: All v1-v10 predecessors remain byte-bound and keep their original claim boundaries.
The repaired transfer contract separates opaque scientific inputs, safe return, cleanup, and Owner-local evaluation from the preserved v5/v6 paths.
REP-DEV is fixed at 150 while 100 Train-250 queries remain reserved for HARNESS-DEV.
P00-P04 have executable specifications, compiler-source commitments, deterministic synthetic tests, and explicit physical-path accounting.
All 25 program-arm receipts are mandatory and all authorization flags and scientific counters remain locked at zero.
weaknesses: Adapter-specific rendered-token feasibility cannot be assessed without the future Owner-local protected transfer and compiled-program manifests.
The live quote, all-fee worst-case charge, provider identity, and remaining authoritative budgets are intentionally pending a separate adoption goal.

strengths: The workload and result contract directly target common-screen quality, unique contribution, latency, storage, determinism, and failures.
weaknesses: No measured result exists because this package is preparation-only.
suggestions: Keep publication claims closed until all 25 aggregate receipts validate.

strengths: Missing lineage, 24-of-25 completion, unsafe transfer, budget overflow, over-length compilation, and non-determinism each have explicit fail-closed outcomes.
weaknesses: Scientific promotion thresholds belong to the later measured-screen decision package, not this preparation request.
suggestions: Bind the unchanged promotion rule before the first measured result is evaluated.

strengths: The claim boundary is limited to request preparation and explicitly excludes retrieval quality and publication claims.
weaknesses: The v9 Qwen observation remains limited to its single-GPU FP16 batch-one scope.
suggestions: Do not generalize v9 synthetic feasibility to multi-program scientific throughput.

strengths: Research plan, protected handoff, transfer, common programs, workloads, result schema, budget, stop rules, and provider admission form a traceable chain.
weaknesses: A separate adoption receipt is still required to bind live identities and Owner-local protected commitments.
suggestions: Require every adoption binding to match the unchanged request hash.

strengths: The initial schema failure and independent-review rejection are retained instead of being erased, and v1-v10 failures remain immutable.
The package freezes five arms, five programs, 150 REP-DEV queries, deterministic compilation, result lineage, resource metrics, and aggregate-only projection.
weaknesses: Per-arm rendered-token feasibility and actual storage/runtime cost remain unobserved until protected local compilation and live admission.
suggestions: Fail adoption unless all 25 compilation bindings report no silent truncation or unresolved over-length input and the full-TTL all-fee quote fits every hard stop.

findings.observation: The logical programs are frozen, but adapter-rendered token lengths, compilation hashes, coverage, and index manifests are not yet available.
findings.reasoning: This is appropriate for a non-adopted preparation request, but it prevents any execution-ready or feasibility claim.
findings.suggestion: Treat the 25 validated compilation bindings and zero unresolved over-length inputs as mandatory adoption prerequisites.
